title: I said "SET" in Korea… and got 3 burgers 🍔🍔🍔 #learnkorean
caption:
세트 (se-teu) = combo meal 🍔🍟🥤
셋 (set) = three — so if you say "burger SET!" in Korea, you might get THREE burgers 😂

Words in this video:
버거 주세요 (beo-geo ju-se-yo) = a burger, please
콜라 주세요 (kol-la ju-se-yo) = a cola, please
아이스크림 (a-i-seu-keu-rim) = ice cream
네 (ne) = yes / sure
세트 주세요 (se-teu ju-se-yo) = a combo, please

Tip: English words in Korean get Korean sounds — burger → 버거 (beo-geo), cola → 콜라 (kol-la).

pinnedComment: What would YOU order? Say it in Korean 👇 (버거? 콜라? 세트? 😆)
alt: A needle-felt miniature burger shop counter. It opens on Mongle, a coral felt ghost-like mascot, staring in shock at three burgers lined up on the counter, with the title How I got 3 burgers. Then from the start: Mongle orders in Korean — 버거 주세요 (a burger, please), 콜라 주세요 (a cola, please), 아이스크림 주세요 (ice cream, please) — and the smiling felt shop worker serves each one. Proud, Mongle says 버거 Set!, meaning a combo meal. The worker raises three fingers: 버거 셋이요? — 셋 means three in Korean. Mongle nods 네!, and three burgers slam down on the counter. Back in the wide shot, Mongle weakly says 세… 세트… 주세요… (a combo… please…). The worker laughs, 아~ 세트! 네~!, and slides over a tray with a burger, fries and a drink. Two labels end it: 셋 set = three, 세트 se-teu = combo.
